THIS PIECE IS BUILT ON THE PERSON'S OWN FILMED VIDEO — the talking-head motion edit of the viral 2026 reels made with Claude (a creator talks to the camera; the edit around them is designed and coded frame by frame). The person did NOT tell you how to cut it: you decide every frame change from their words, like a top editor would. Nobody has to ask for a split screen or icons — you bring them where the words call for them.

THE NON-NEGOTIABLES
1. Their video is the spine. It plays IN SYNC from 0 to the end (K.footage.draw always shows the frame of now — never re-time it, never freeze it, never reverse it): their lips must match their voice. The piece lasts exactly the video's length. Their voice IS the soundtrack (it is mixed in for you, under nothing): never write words to be read aloud, and keep your effects under it.
2. The frame changes WITH THE WORDS. Every change lands on a word boundary from the timed words (a change starts 0.1–0.2 s before the key word, so the picture arrives as the word is said). Never two changes inside 1.2 s; never a hold longer than ~5 s without something new (a push-in, a word typed beside them, a change of frame).
3. Every shot names how their video sits ("frame" in the plan) — and two shots in a row never use the same one:
   • full — they fill the frame (cover, the face kept in), with a slow push-in (zoom 1.00 → 1.06 over the shot) or a punch-in on a key word (zoom 1.25 in 0.25 s, eased).
   • card — their video shrinks into a floating rounded card (radius ≈ 3–4% of the frame, a soft long shadow, kept FLAT — never tilted into 3D to fake depth; depth comes from a motivated camera move) on a DESIGNED STAGE (a soft gradient or paper ground, a grid or a glow — no HUD rows, no corner marks, no labels that are not the content itself), with the key line typed beside or under it.
   • split — the frame is cut in two (portrait: top/bottom; landscape: left/right): they are in one half with the face centred in it, the explainer is drawn in the other; the divide moves in on a spring and leaves on one.
   • corner — they become a small circle or rounded box in a corner (face filling it) while the explainer fills the rest.
   • away — they disappear (the voice goes on) and a FULL-SCREEN motion explainer shows what they are saying: tool icons drawn in code on rounded tiles assembling into a grid, a timeline of clips sliding in, an easing curve drawing itself, a chart growing, a phone UI, a number counting, a before/after. 1.5–3.5 s, then they come back (the card flies back in and grows to full, a zoom through the explainer, a mask wipe on the beat).
   • over — they stay full and kinetic words appear beside them (never on the face: K.footage.draw returns where the face landed; keep text out of that box with a margin).
4. They are seen talking most of the time: at least half of the piece shows their face (full, card, split, corner or over); open on them (or on a hook that cuts to them inside 1.5 s). THE ENDING: their last line on them, then a short clean end card (1.5–2.5 s): the one idea of the piece in their words, centred on the stage, no person, held still (their voice may finish under it).
5. The explainers come FROM THEIR WORDS. When they name a thing (a tool, an app, a place, a number, a list, a step, a before/after), show it — never decoration for its own sake. Generic icons are drawn in code (rounded tiles, line icons, real shapes), never emoji. NEVER draw another company's logo or app icon: a named app or brand is its NAME written in type on a plain labelled tile (with a generic icon for its kind — a camera for a photo app, a play triangle for a video app). Never write computer-vision labels or tracking tags on their real video. A number they say counts up as they say it. A list they say builds item by item on each item's word.
6. On-screen words are THEIR key words, exactly as they said them (Arabic as spoken; another language as spoken) — a headline of 1–5 words per moment, mixing a heavy weight with a light or italic one, typed or masked in on the word. Not full captions.
7. Whenever they are shown, their WHOLE FACE is inside the visible part (K.footage.draw keeps it in by default), never cut by a panel's edge, never under text, never under the platform's buttons (portrait: keep the face above 0.78 of H).
8. Transitions are motion, not cuts: the card scales and slides on K.ease.silk / springs (8–16 frames), the divide sweeps, a blur-to-sharp, a mask wipe; one whoosh / pop on each change, soft under the voice.
9. One designed world for the whole piece: one stage, one palette (3–5 colours, one accent), the same two fonts, the same UI language on every panel — the variety is in the frames and the motion, not in the style.
10. Rhythm by intensity: 1–2 → a change every 4–6 s, mostly full/card; 3 → every 3–4 s; 4–5 → every 2–3 s with "away" explainers on the big words.

quality_bar.million_dollar_bar_and_cheap_look_blackl:
THE OWNER'S BAR — «لو حطيت المقطع، الشخص يفكر مصروف عليه ملايين»: a viewer must believe millions were spent on it. Not a pleasant template: a studio piece. Aim there on every shot.

WHAT MAKES IT LOOK EXPENSIVE (numbers from the research; apply them, don't recite them)
- Easing: never linear on anything that starts or stops. Entrances K.ease.silk / outExpo / outQuint (80% of the way fast, a long landing); exits inCubic, 60–75% of the entrance's length; state-to-state inOutCubic. No more than two tweens of a shot on the same ease. Never start a shot at its t = 0 exactly (offset 0.1–0.3 s).
- Durations: small element 0.4–0.7 s, headline build 0.6–1.0 s, hero reveal 1.2–2.5 s, camera moves 3–6 s across the shot; longer for longer distances. Energy 0.15–0.3 s, luxury 0.5–0.8 s, cinematic 0.8–2 s. The slowest shot ≥ 3× the fastest.
- Overshoot budget: premium/brand 0–2%; feedback 2–5%; a badge 5–10% (0 → 1.08 → 1); never on opacity. Springs: damping near critical by default; bouncy only when the brand is playful. Never scale from 0 — from 0.9–0.97 with opacity, or build it from particles/masks.
- Stagger: letters (Latin only) 15–35 ms, UI 30–80 ms, words 60–120 ms, dramatic 100–200 ms; a group's whole stagger ≤ 0.5–0.7 s.
- Choreography: ONE hero motion at a time; at most 2–3 secondary motions at lower amplitude; at most a third of the elements moving at once; the background always slightly alive (0.5–2% drift, slow noise, dust). Shot shape: build 0–30%, breathe 30–70% with exactly one ambient motion (scale 1 → 1.04), resolve 70–100%. Follow-through: children 50–150 ms behind; the background counter-moves 20–30%.
- Premium = ONE object changing shape across shots (a word dissolves into the dust that builds the next one; a card grows into the next scene; a line becomes the chart). A crossfade between pictures looks cheap.
- Camera: a slow push (2–6% scale) on every hold; parallax with 3–5 planes (near 1.5×, hero 1×, far 0.2–0.4×) via K.camera + K.inSpace with dof; rack focus 0.4–0.8 s; orbits slow (15–40° over 4–6 s); crash zoom 0.2–0.4 s with motion blur only for a punch; never shake or spin without a reason; the lens (fov) does not tween.
- Light & finish: a key glow or rim on the hero, a MOVING specular (K.lightSweep once per ~3 s at most), restrained bloom (strength 0.2–0.6), vignette 10–25%, grain light or none (K.grain default 0.02, never above 0.04 — the owner's «убери шум»), RGB split 0.5–1.5 px only on hits. Contact shadows under floating things.
- Type: one idea per card (≤ 7 words), held ≥ 1.5 s after it lands (0.5 s + 0.25 s a word); headline ≥ 8% of the frame's width in px (≈ 90–180 px at 1080), support ≥ 4%, nothing under 3.3%; hero text 60–80% of the width; weight contrast 300/400 vs 800/900; ≤ 2 families; mask reveals rising 40–60% of their height (outExpo 0.6–0.9 s); blur-to-sharp 8–16 px → 0 with 4–8% scale-down. Never typewriter on headlines, never bouncing letters, never spinning 3D text.
- Colour: 3–5 colours, ONE accent (60-30-10) on the hero / key word only; near-black (#0a0a0c–#141318) and off-white (#f2f0eb) instead of pure black/white; one grade for the whole piece. Brand colours win when given.
- Pacing: the hook in the first 1–1.5 s (an impossible event on frame 1); something new every 0.8–1.5 s (kinetic) or 2–4 s (explainer); cuts on the beat grid; the biggest reveal on the drop after a riser; the ending held ≥ 2 s or looping into frame 1 (make the last 0.5 s match the start).
- Sound (cues): whoosh 10–20 ms before the move, impact on the exact landing frame, riser cresting on the reveal, soft UI ticks for small things; ~1 accent per 1–2 s; never the same cue twice in a row; no hit on every word.

THE CHEAP-LOOK BLACKLIST (a critic rejects the piece for any of these)
centred title on a gradient with everything fading in · linear slides · one ease and one duration for everything · bouncy overshoot on a premium brand · particle bursts or glows for no reason ("AI purple") · crossfades, star wipes, page curls, random wipes, glitch on every cut, constant zoom, spinning cards · a static or empty opening, a logo intro · dead frames (nothing alive for > 1 s) · text overlapping another text during a swap, text blurred by scaling, text under the platform's buttons, text < 3.3% of the width · invented UI, invented numbers, the brand typed as text when its logo was given · pure #000 / #fff · rainbow gradients, > 2 fonts, outlines and bevels on type · over-bloom that washes the frame, heavy RGB split everywhere, gradient banding · objects floating with no grounding · living beings drawn as shapes (use given pictures instead) · a loop that stutters, a single-frame pop.

ARABIC (over anything above written for Latin type)
Animate whole words or lines, never letters (the joins break); never letter-spacing (K.text never tracks Arabic) — stretch with kashida (ـ) only after letters that join forward; motion, masks, wipes and lists run RIGHT → LEFT (the first item on the right); line height 1.3–1.5 with room above for diacritics; one digit system (Western 0–9 unless asked for ٠١٢: K.digits / K.counter {arabic:true}); Arabic 10–15% larger than Latin for the same read. Word-by-word 120–200 ms a word, 60–120 ms apart; pill 300–450 ms; badge pop 350–500 ms (0 → 1.08 → 1, −8° → 0); a hold over 2.5 s needs a secondary motion; end card 3–7 s. Gulf campaigns: gold/brass on deep dark grounds, geometric patterns assembling from particles.

scene_program.contract:
THE SCENE YOU WRITE — one JavaScript program (no HTML, no imports) that calls scene() once:

scene({
  title: "…",                     // the piece's name
  duration: 15,                   // seconds (the brief's length)
  bpm: 120,                       // the tempo the beats sit on (cuts and hits land on its grid)
  background: "#0b0b10",          // filled before every frame (optional)
  blur: 0.5,                      // motion-blur shutter 0–1 (0.5 = 180°): averaged sub-frames on export; 0 for crisp UI
  three: false,                   // true → K.THREE (three.js 0.170.0) and K.addon("postprocessing/EffectComposer.js") are loaded; render into K.glCanvas and draw it onto ctx
  cues: [ { t: 0.0, sfx: "transition-whoosh-fast" }, { t: 1.2, sfx: "hit-bass-hit", vol: 0.8 } ], // sound on the frames that change

viral_formats:
VIRAL FORMATS YOU CAN BUILD (pick from these or invent your own from the same principles — never a template look)
1. DUST TO WORD — thousands of particles (K.textPoints → K.swarm, from "edge"/"scatter", wave right→left for Arabic) fly on a curl flow and lock into the key word; a light sweep crosses it; bloom; then it blows away (p 1→0, from "explode") into the next shot. Hook on frame 1.
2. ONE SHAPE, NEVER CUT — a single rounded shape morphs through 6–12 states (pill → card → chart → badge → logo) with K.springTo on size, radius and colour; its content swaps with a short blur; a camera keeps each state filling the frame; the last frame equals the first (loop).
3. LIQUID TITLE — K.metaballs in the brand gradient breathing behind (or forming) the title, glass cards (K.glass) floating over it with real numbers (K.counter), a slow orbit of the light.
4. 2.5D FLY-THROUGH — 4–5 depth planes (far haze, mid shapes, hero type, near dust) through K.camera/K.inSpace with depth of field; the camera dives through the hero word into the next world (portal transition); speed ramp: fast → slow on the reveal → fast.
5. KINETIC TYPE ON THE BEAT — one idea per beat on a 120 BPM grid: mask reveals rising from a line, a heavy key word (2–4× the filler, the accent colour, a glow) against thin filler words, word swaps in the same slot, a counter rolling on ticks, a hard cut on every bar.
6. PRODUCT / LOGO HERO — the given picture alone on a seamless ground sampled from its own colour, 60–70% of the frame, a slow orbit-like parallax, a specular sweep, an impact burst of particles frozen mid-air (bullet time: the particles stop while the camera keeps moving), contact shadow.
7. DATA THAT FEELS PHYSICAL — bars and rings that grow on springs, a line that draws itself (K.drawOn) and becomes the next shape, numbers counting up on ticks, glass labels, one highlighted fact.
8. INFINITE ZOOM — each scene is drawn inside the previous one (a window, a pupil, a dot); the camera zooms forever through them; the last scene contains the first (loop). Everything stays sharp at every scale.
9. MIXED-MEDIA COLLAGE — the given photos as torn/cut paper layers at depths, halftone or two-colour grade, tape and marker type, a stop-motion step (hold each pose 2 frames) for a handmade feel.
10. DISINTEGRATE TRANSITION — a picture or word dissolves into dust (K.imagePoints / K.textPoints with ownColor, p 1→0, from "explode", curl high) that drifts and re-forms as the next element.
Camera moves to borrow (as 2.5D): crash zoom, push-in, dolly zoom (scale the hero against the background in opposite directions), orbit-parallax, whip pan (horizontal motion blur + echo), top-down dive, through-object portal, speed ramp, rack focus.

footage.skill:
THIS PIECE IS BUILT ON THE PERSON'S OWN FILMED VIDEO — the talking-head motion edit of the viral 2026 reels made with Claude (a creator talks to the camera; the edit around them is designed and coded frame by frame). The person did NOT tell you how to cut it: you decide every frame change from their words, like a top editor would. Nobody has to ask for a split screen or icons — you bring them where the words call for them.

THE NON-NEGOTIABLES
1. Their video is the spine. It plays IN SYNC from 0 to the end (K.footage.draw always shows the frame of now — never re-time it, never freeze it, never reverse it): their lips must match their voice. The piece lasts exactly the video's length. Their voice IS the soundtrack (it is mixed in for you, under nothing): never write words to be read aloud, and keep your effects under it.
2. The frame changes WITH THE WORDS. Every change lands on a word boundary from the timed words (a change starts 0.1–0.2 s before the key word, so the picture arrives as the word is said). Never two changes inside 1.2 s; never a hold longer than ~5 s without something new (a push-in, a word typed beside them, a change of frame).
3. Every shot names how their video sits ("frame" in the plan) — and two shots in a row never use the same one:
   • full — they fill the frame (cover, the face kept in), with a slow push-in (zoom 1.00 → 1.06 over the shot) or a punch-in on a key word (zoom 1.25 in 0.25 s, eased).
   • card — their video shrinks into a floating rounded card (radius ≈ 3–4% of the frame, a soft long shadow, kept FLAT — never tilted into 3D to fake depth; depth comes from a motivated camera move) on a DESIGNED STAGE (a soft gradient or paper ground, a grid or a glow — no HUD rows, no corner marks, no labels that are not the content itself), with the key line typed beside or under it.
   • split — the frame is cut in two (portrait: top/bottom; landscape: left/right): they are in one half with the face centred in it, the explainer is drawn in the other; the divide moves in on a spring and leaves on one.
   • corner — they become a small circle or rounded box in a corner (face filling it) while the explainer fills the rest.
   • away — they disappear (the voice goes on) and a FULL-SCREEN motion explainer shows what they are saying: tool icons drawn in code on rounded tiles assembling into a grid, a timeline of clips sliding in, an easing curve drawing itself, a chart growing, a phone UI, a number counting, a before/after. 1.5–3.5 s, then they come back (the card flies back in and grows to full, a zoom through the explainer, a mask wipe on the beat).
   • over — they stay full and kinetic words appear beside them (never on the face: K.footage.draw returns where the face landed; keep text out of that box with a margin).
4. They are seen talking most of the time: at least half of the piece shows their face (full, card, split, corner or over); open on them (or on a hook that cuts to them inside 1.5 s). THE ENDING: their last line on them, then a short clean end card (1.5–2.5 s): the one idea of the piece in their words, centred on the stage, no person, held still (their voice may finish under it).
5. The explainers come FROM THEIR WORDS. When they name a thing (a tool, an app, a place, a number, a list, a step, a before/after), show it — never decoration for its own sake. Generic icons are drawn in code (rounded tiles, line icons, real shapes), never emoji. NEVER draw another company's logo or app icon: a named app or brand is its NAME written in type on a plain labelled tile (with a generic icon for its kind — a camera for a photo app, a play triangle for a video app). Never write computer-vision labels or tracking tags on their real video. A number they say counts up as they say it. A list they say builds item by item on each item's word.
6. On-screen words are THEIR key words, exactly as they said them (Arabic as spoken; another language as spoken) — a headline of 1–5 words per moment, mixing a heavy weight with a light or italic one, typed or masked in on the word. Not full captions.
7. Whenever they are shown, their WHOLE FACE is inside the visible part (K.footage.draw keeps it in by default), never cut by a panel's edge, never under text, never under the platform's buttons (portrait: keep the face above 0.78 of H).
8. Transitions are motion, not cuts: the card scales and slides on K.ease.silk / springs (8–16 frames), the divide sweeps, a blur-to-sharp, a mask wipe; one whoosh / pop on each change, soft under the voice.
9. One designed world for the whole piece: one stage, one palette (3–5 colours, one accent), the same two fonts, the same UI language on every panel — the variety is in the frames and the motion, not in the style.
10. Rhythm by intensity: 1–2 → a change every 4–6 s, mostly full/card; 3 → every 3–4 s; 4–5 → every 2–3 s with "away" explainers on the big words.
footage.kit_api:
THE PERSON'S VIDEO IN THE KIT — K.footage (null when there is none):
K.footage.draw(ctx, x, y, w, h, { zoom=1 (1 = cover; >1 punches in on the face), radius=0, circle=false, shadow=false|true|px, shadowColor, alpha=1, border=0, borderColor, cx, cy (0..1: crop centre instead of the face), fit:"cover"|"contain" }) → the face's box where it landed {x,y,w,h} in canvas pixels (keep text out of it). It draws the video's frame of NOW (the runtime hands it in for every frame — you never seek it). Draw it inside ctx.save()/transforms like any picture: rotate, skew or scale the ctx around it for a tilted floating card.
K.footage.full(ctx, {zoom, cx, cy}) → the same, filling the frame.
K.footage.faceAt(t) → {x,y,w,h} the face's centre and size in fractions of the video's picture (smoothed between the measured moments).
K.footage.wordAt(t) → {w,s,e} the word being said at t, or null · K.footage.words → every word [{w,s,e}] (seconds) · K.footage.lines → spoken lines [{text,from,to}] · K.footage.w / .h (its picture size) · K.footage.duration.
Draw the video with K.footage.draw — never with K.img or drawImage on K.footage.frame yourself (it would lose the face framing).
footage.person_api: THE PERSON IS CUT OUT TOO (K.footage.hasPerson = true): K.footage.draw(ctx, x, y, w, h, { …the same options…, person: true }) draws ONLY the person (hair and all, transparent around them) with exactly the crop the plain draw uses. That is the "words behind the head" look of the viral reels: draw the video (or the stage), then the big key word, then the same draw with person:true on top — the word sits BEHIND them. Use it on 1–3 moments (a hook word, the big idea), never on every shot; on a designed stage you may also drop their room entirely (stage, then the person alone). Keep the face uncovered as always.

# الكفر والثمبنيل — اللي ينقرا بالجوال

**المحرّك مشترك** مع سكل الريل. كل `scripts/` و`references/` من هني:
`${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../video-ad-editor`

**اقرأ أول شي:** `references/thumbnails.md` — الأحجام الدنيا ومصادرها. الشبكة تصغّر الكفر لـ12٪، فاللي تحت الحد ما ينقرا.

## قبل ما تبدأ — سؤال واحد
**«آخذ صورتك من الفيديو، ولا عندك صور تعطيني؟»**
- **من الفيديو:** السكربت يختار أوضح فريم ووجهك كبير فيه، ويقصّك على خلفية كريمية (`--cut` للكفر · `--video` للثمبنيل — يحتاج ماك).
- **صورك:** صورة مقصوصة بخلفية شفافة (`--photo`) — الأحسن للثمبنيل: انفعال واضح (ابتسامة كبيرة، دهشة).
- لو ما رد: من الفيديو.

**التصميم من موضوع الفيديو كل مرة — مو قالب:** العنوان من كلامه، والشعارات/العناصر من اللي يتكلم عنه (أداة، شركة، رقم). الهيكل ثابت والمحتوى يتغيّر.
**الخلفية كريمية مثل كلود** (`#F0EEE6`، أو `bg` الثيم لو فاتح) — `--bg` يغيّرها، و`--bg video` ياخذ لون خلفية الفيديو.

## كفر الريل (9:16) — ويصير أول فريم بالفيديو

```bash
python3 scripts/28_cover.py <work> "سطر|*كلمة مميزة*" [--photo me.png | --cut] [--x قديم.png --ok جديد.png] [--first ad-master.mp4]
python3 scripts/34_phone_preview.py <work>/cover.jpg
```

- كل المهم داخل مربع 1:1 بالنص — وهمي، بلا إطار.
- العنوان 5 كلمات بالكثير، سطرين، ≈9 أحرف بالسطر (السكربت ينبّهك).
- ✕ و✓ **مو قاعدة** — بس لو الفيديو «من كذا لكذا». الشعارات صف فوق الراس داخل المربع، والكلام تحت على الصدر.
- `--first` يركّب الكفر أول فريم ← `<الاسم>-cover.mp4`.
- اعرض `cover_phone.jpg` (بحجمه الحقيقي بالجوال) — لو ما قريته فيها، ما ينقرا.

## ثمبنيل يوتيوب (16:9) — ثلاث أفكار

```bash
python3 scripts/33_thumb.py <work> "سطر|*كلمة مميزة*" [--photo me.png | --video src.mov] [--logo شي.png] [--x قديم.png --ok جديد.png]
python3 scripts/34_phone_preview.py <work>/thumb_A_1280.jpg --youtube
```

- يطلّع 3840×2160 (الموصى) + 1280×720 (للجوال، أقل من 2 ميقا) لكل فكرة، وورقة `thumbs_sheet.jpg` — اعرضها وخلّه يختار.
- الوجه كبير بانفعال واضح · تحت يمين فاضي (مدة الفيديو) · 3-5 كلمات.

## ⛔ أسلوبك

- العنوان من محتوى الفيديو نفسه — هوك مختصر، لا تخترع كلام ما قاله.
- ولا كلمة على الوجه. الخطوط Cairo (أو خط ثيمه).
- اعرض الصورة قبل أي رفع أو نشر — لا نشر ولا جدولة.

# قواعد الكفر والثمبنيل — اللي ينقرا بشاشة الجوال

بحث 3 أكتوبر 2026 + قياس لقطة شاشة ماجد (آيفون، تبويب الريلز). كل رقم معلّم: **مؤكد** (له مصدر) · **محسوب** (الحسبة معروضة) · **رأي**.

## ليش الكفر «ما يبين من بعيد»؟
- شبكة البروفايل تصغّر الكفر لـ**12٪** من حجمه: كفر عرضه 1080 يصير مربّع 130 نقطة بجوال 393 (**مؤكد بالقياس**). بجوال ماجد 146 نقطة (13.5٪).
- أصغر خط مقروء بالآيفون **11 نقطة**، والعادي **17** (**مؤكد** — Apple HIG).
- ⇒ نص 11 نقطة يحتاج **91 بكسل** بالكفر، و17 نقطة **141 بكسل** (**محسوب**: النقاط ÷ 0.1204).
- العربي يبين أصغر من اللاتيني بنفس الحجم (**مؤكد** — Thomas Phinney) ⇒ نكبّره ×1.2 (**تقدير**).
- كفر زورجا الأول: العنوان طلع ≈13 نقطة، والسطر الصغير ≈6، وكلام الشعارات ≈5، والحساب ≈4 — كلها تحت الحد.

---

## 🎬 كفر الريل (1080×1920) — ويتركّب أول فريم بالفيديو

| القاعدة | الرقم | الدرجة |
|---|---|---|
| المنطقة الآمنة | كل المهم بمربع 1:1 بالنص (y من 420 لين 1500) — وهمي، بلا إطار | قرار ماجد (أضيق من 4:5 و3:4 فيضمنهم) |
| الشبكة | البروفايل يقص 3:4 من النص (y 240-1680)، الفيد 4:5 (y 285-1635)، تبويب الريلز 9:16 كامل | مؤكد (3:4) · مرجّح (4:5) |
| العنوان العربي | **170 بكسل أقل شي** (أحسن 190-230) | محسوب |
| أي نص ثاني | **110 بكسل أقل شي** — ولا شي تحت 91 | محسوب |
| الكلمات | **5 بالكثير**، سطرين، **9 أحرف تقريباً بالسطر** عند 170 | رأي + محسوب (كايرو 900 ≈ 0.62 من الحجم للحرف) |
| الشعار / الأيقونة | **200 بكسل أقل شي** | محسوب (24 نقطة) |
| الخطوط والحدود | **10 بكسل أقل شي** (الأرفع يختفي) | محسوب |
| الوزن | Bold أو Black — لا Light ولا Thin، ولا تباعد حروف بالعربي | مؤكد (HIG) · رأي |
| التباين | 4.5:1 (أو 3:1 للنص الضخم) | مرجّح (WCAG) |
| الحساب `@handle` | **لا** — ما ينقرا ومكانه البروفايل أصلاً | محسوب |

**الترتيب داخل المربع:** (عناصر الخبر فوق لو فيه) ← الوجه ← العنوان تحت على الصدر. ولا كلمة على الوجه.
**الشعارات:** حسب العنوان — مو قاعدة. ✕ على اللي تركته و✓ على البديل **بس** لو الخبر «من كذا لكذا».
**الفحص:** `python3 scripts/34_phone_preview.py <work>/cover.jpg` — يطلّع الكفر بحجمه الحقيقي (تبويب الريلز · البروفايل · من بعيد). لو ما قريته بالمعاينة، ما ينقرا بالجوال.

---

## ▶️ ثمبنيل يوتيوب (16:9)

| القاعدة | الرقم | الدرجة |
|---|---|---|
| المقاس | **3840×2160** الموصى (أقل شي عرض 640)، ونطلّع معاه 1280×720. الحجم أقل من 2 ميقا للرفع من الجوال | مؤكد (YouTube Help 72431) |
| الفيديو العمودي | يوتيوب يولّد له ثمبنيل 4:5 بالرئيسية — خلّ المهم بالنص | مؤكد |
| أصغر عرض | الجانبي (المقترح) 218×123 بالكمبيوتر ← المقياس 0.17 | مؤكد بالقياس |
| النص العربي (على 1280) | **120 بكسل أقل شي** (100 للاتيني) | محسوب |
| الشعار / الأيقونة (على 1280) | **140 بكسل أقل شي** | محسوب |
| تحت يمين | **310×145 فاضي** — مكان مدة الفيديو | محسوب من القياس |
| الكلمات | 3-5 | رأي |
| الوجه | انفعال واضح (دهشة، ابتسامة كبيرة)، والوجه كبير | مؤكد (نصايح يوتيوب: «shocked face») |
| البساطة | فكرة وحدة، «لا تعقّد التصميم»، خط واضح | مؤكد |

**3 نسخ:** كل ثمبنيل يطلع بثلاث أفكار مختلفة (وجه + كلمة · وجه + شي من الخبر · قبل/بعد) ويختار هو.
**الفحص:** `python3 scripts/34_phone_preview.py thumb.jpg --youtube` — الرئيسية بالجوال + الجانبي الصغير + مكان المدة.

---

## الصورة والخلفية (قرار ماجد 3 أكتوبر)
- **اسأل أول:** «آخذ صورتك من الفيديو، ولا عندك صور تعطيني؟» — من الفيديو: `_cutout.py` يختار الفريم (أكبر وجه × أوضح صورة) ويقصّ الشخص بـVision (ماك). الوجه من الفيديو عادةً بلا انفعال، فالصورة منه أضعف للثمبنيل — قله.
- **الخلفية كريمية مثل كلود** `#F0EEE6` والأطراف أغمق 8-10٪ (مو أسود) · الكلام غامق `#1F1F1D` بالثمبنيل · بالكفر الكلام أبيض على الصدر (القميص الغامق) — ولا ظل غامق على الكريمي.
- **الصورة من الفيديو بالكفر:** الجسم مقطوع عند الصدر — الذقن فوق العنوان (≈1000) والأطراف تذوب بالخلفية.

## الخطوط (موحّدة)
- **Cairo** لكل العربي (900 للعنوان، 800 للسطر الصغير) · **IBM Plex Mono** للإنقليزي الصغير بس.
- الثيم (`theme.json ← font`) يغلب لو المستخدم اختار خط بصفحة التعارف.

## المصادر
- Apple HIG Typography — developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography
- شبكة انستقرام 3:4 (يناير 2025) — petapixel.com/2025/01/23/instagram-swaps-square-profile-grids-for-rectangles
- YouTube thumbnails — support.google.com/youtube/answer/72431 · support.google.com/youtube/answer/12340300
